10. PEtab import and export

Source: vignettes/articles/guide-petab.Rmd
guide-petab.Rmd

PEtab is the exchange format for ODE parameter estimation problems: an SBML model plus tables of measurements, observables with noise models, conditions, and parameters with scales and bounds, joined by a YAML file. This chapter writes the guide model at the best fit as a PEtab problem and reads it back (petab.R); problems of the PEtab benchmark collection and other tools are read the same way.

PEtab export

exportPEtab() writes reactions as SBML, observables, errors, data, and the transformation p with scales, fixed values and values per condition. A parameter entering only as exp() is on log scale. PEtab 2, the default, has no parameter scales: values are written on linear scale, with a warning listing the log-scale parameters. The gauge of Symmetries becomes fixed values, also linear.

  • State at rest. With steadyState = pSS, each condition starts with a pre-equilibration to steady state before time 0. The totals of the conserved moieties (the Pimpl() parameters) become initial-value parameters: one species per total starts at the total, here complex NfkIkb for NFκB and unphosphorylated Ikk for IKK, all others at 0; the simulation preserves the totals. Both conditions differ only in the dose, given by the event, and share one pre-equilibration condition.
  • Event. With events = events, the event at time 0 becomes the TNF value in the condition table, set after pre-equilibration.
  • Errors. Imaging readouts get their error model; the blots, outside the error model, get the data standard deviations as noise parameters per measurement, as in normL2().
# the estimated parameters at the best fit, the gauge as fixed values on the linear scale of the
# model
best <- as.parvec(readRDS("results/fits.rds"))
yaml <- exportPEtab(data, reactions, observables = g, p = p, pouter = best, errors = e,
                    fixed = exp(gauge), steadyState = pSS, events = events,
                    modelID = "oppelt", dir = "results/petab", overwrite = TRUE)
list.files("results/petab")
#> [1] "conditions_oppelt.tsv"   "experiments_oppelt.tsv" 
#> [3] "measurements_oppelt.tsv" "observables_oppelt.tsv" 
#> [5] "oppelt.xml"              "oppelt.yaml"            
#> [7] "parameters_oppelt.tsv"

Each experiment starts with the pre-equilibration at \(t = -\infty\), then the experiment condition at 0:

read.delim("results/petab/experiments_oppelt.tsv")
#>                experimentId time conditionId
#> 1     preequilibration__TNF -Inf            
#> 2     preequilibration__TNF    0         TNF
#> 3 preequilibration__control -Inf            
#> 4 preequilibration__control    0     control
read.delim("results/petab/conditions_oppelt.tsv")
#>   conditionId targetId targetValue
#> 1         TNF      TNF           1
#> 2     control      TNF           0

PEtab import

importPEtab() builds prdfn, the obsfns of observables and errors, the parfn with the scales of the parameter table, data and objfn. A pre-equilibration becomes a Pimpl() with totals from the initial values. options go to the solver; with compile = FALSE, compile() builds the sources.

petab <- importPEtab(yaml, backend = "cppDE", options = list(atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8),
                     modelname = "oppelt_petab", compile = FALSE)
compile(petab$prd, petab$e, output = "oppelt_petab", cores = 6)
# the data term of model.R and the objective of the problem read back
c(model.R = attr(obj(c(best, gauge), deriv = FALSE), "data"),
  PEtab   = petab$obj(petab$bestfit, deriv = FALSE)$value)
#>   model.R     PEtab 
#> -511.1623 -511.1623

The imported problem reproduces the data term of model.R at the best fit. petab$bestfit has the nominal values on the problem scales, petab$parlower and petab$parupper the bounds; it is fitted and profiled like any other.

SBML models

exportSbml() writes species with compartments and volumes, reactions with kinetic laws, parameters and initial assignments, here one species per total set to that total. SBML kinetic laws are amounts per time: exportSbml() multiplies concentration rates by the compartment volume, importSbml() divides again. importSbml() returns an equation list with compartments, volumes, parameter values, initial values, assignment rules and events:

sbml <- importSbml("results/petab/oppelt.xml")
names(sbml)
#> [1] "reactions"       "pars"            "inits"           "observables"    
#> [5] "assignmentRules" "events"          "eventsSource"    "renamed"
c(states = length(sbml$reactions$states), reactions = length(sbml$reactions$rates))
#>    states reactions 
#>        23        38
identical(sort(sbml$reactions$states), sort(reactions$states))
#> [1] TRUE

exportSbml(reactions, parameters, inits, filepath) writes an equation list without PEtab tables.

Formats and limits

  • SBML and PEtab run through reticulate with python-libsbml; DMOD_LIBSBML_PYTHON selects the interpreter.
  • PEtab 1 and 2 are read. exportPEtab() writes 2 by default, 1 with formatVersion = "1", which keeps scales but puts expressions into the condition table that only dMod2 reads.
  • exportPEtab() writes events at time 0 that replace a state and refuses others.

Reference: exportPEtab(), importPEtab(), exportSbml(), importSbml()
